rootRulingMA1.verbatim:
## 2026-10-28 Root ruling: A2 gating mutant MA1 survived (assertion removal)

Facts (from _reports/2026-10-28/a2-impl/STOPPED.json, head 04d9f2d42): GREEN built run 26/26 on the first attempt. MA1 removes the actor reply id from `ids = new Set([acted.reply.event?.id, seen.frame.event.id])` in concurrent-first-sockets. It passed 26/26. The worker correctly found it is not equivalent, and stopped.

Root reading: MA1 deletes an assertion. On a correct product the actor's reply and the guest's delivery carry the same event id, so no run on an unmutated server can kill it. This is a gap in how the mutant was specified at admission, not a missing harness check. The fault classes differ:
- A MatchHostRegistry race (two hosts for one match) is caught before the equality check: the guest's intentId-correlated waitFor times out.
- The equality check exists only for id divergence: the guest receives the same intent's event under a different id than the actor's reply.

Ruling: discharge MA1 as a paired (combined) mutant, the method CF-A2M-1 already asks for on R6.
1. Build one image with a product mutant PA1, so that the guest-visible event id diverges from the actor's reply id for the same intent.
   - It goes at the narrowest seam (for example the publish/broadcast envelope in ServerMatchHostPublication.ts or ServerMatchHostCommandResults.ts).
   - If it breaks an earlier row, scope it to the cfs match. Disclose the scoping.
   - PA1 is scratch only. It is never committed and is restored byte-exact afterwards.
2. Run the unmutated A2 harness against PA1. Required: concurrent-first-sockets fails on the named check "concurrent first sockets conflicted", with two ids. A failure at an earlier row or a different check does not count.
3. Run the MA1 harness against the same PA1 image, without a rebuild. Required: concurrent-first-sockets passes, which shows MA1's deleted assertion was the only thing that caught PA1.
4. Record MA1 as killed in combination, with PA1 as its witness, and disclose it as such. It is not a plain kill.

If no single-seam PA1 can make the ids diverge without breaking the build, stop and report. Root will then rule MA1 a disclosed survivor (R6 precedent). MA2-MA5 continue under the unchanged rule: a survivor stops the unit unless shown equivalent.

## 2026-10-28 Root ruling: A2 mutant MA3 survived (co-op unit command ownership is a known, registered gap), and MA2 qualification

Facts (from _reports/2026-10-28/a2-impl/ma3-analysis.json, head 0175450f1):
- MA3 sends the post-restart Move for a2-u1, owned by pid_5mtAz6..., on the other contributor's connection (pid_BgZdaK..., same `player` side).
- The built server accepted it: movement_declared, intentId coop-two-2-1. All 4 owned rows passed.

Root reading:
- On main, `refuseForeignUnitCommand` in src/lib/multiplayer/server/ServerMatchHostIntent.ts returns early for every co-op campaign match (`if (meta?.coopCampaign) return null;`, comment at :559-566: "Until that map reaches the host, co-op unit commands are unconstrained").
- The fix is already registered: units.json U38 (node R2.authority-live, state blocked). It deletes that exemption and refuses a teammate commanding another player's unit with AUTH_REJECTED unit-not-owned. It applies the owner's earlier answer "control only their own units" (docs/audits/2026-10-17-l1-amendment-draft.md row 17 -> U38).
- So MA3 asserted behaviour main does not yet have. This is not a new owner policy question and not a new product finding: it is the known gap U38 owns. A2 may not edit product code, and its admission does not claim per-unit command ownership.

Ruling:
1. MA3 is reclassified from gating to a known-gap witness. Record it as "SURVIVED: expected on main; co-op per-unit command ownership is not enforced until U38". It is not an A2 defect, and it does not count as a kill.
2. CF-A2-1, new and open: co-op teammate unit commands are unconstrained on main (witness: the MA3 built run on BUILD_ID 1793172695427). Owner: U38. When U38 lands, its proof must include a built-image row equivalent to MA3 that is refused.
   - Disclosure: the A2 local receipt, the PR body, and the release-notes known issue via RELEASE-PRODUCER-1 (G-A9 list).
   - No A2 text may claim that only the unit owner can move.
3. MA2 counts as killed by the named node:test source-order assertion (pure level). Its built-image failure (ECONNREFUSED) is not a named check: disclose it, and do not count it as a built kill.
4. MA4 and MA5 continue under the unchanged rule: a survivor stops the unit unless shown equivalent, or unless it is shown to be the same registered gap, which Root rules.

## 2026-10-28 Root ruling: A2 mutant MA5 survived (assertion removal, same class as MA1)

Facts: MA5 deletes the journal gap/duplicate assertion (`row.eventCount === row.maxSequence + 1`) after the concurrent round in concurrent-first-sockets. It passed all 4 owned rows on BUILD_ID 1793172695427 (head 2581096fb). The worker correctly found it is not equivalent.

Ruling: same method as MA1.
1. Build one scratch image with a product mutant PA5 that leaves a journal gap or a duplicate sequence for the cfs match during the concurrent round, at the narrowest append seam (for example the sequence assignment in the match journal append path).
   - Scope it to the cfs match and disclose that.
   - Never commit it; restore it byte-exact.
2. Run the unmutated harness. concurrent-first-sockets must fail on "journal has a gap or duplicate".
3. Run the MA5 harness on the same image, without a rebuild. concurrent-first-sockets must pass.
4. Record MA5 as "killed in combination (witness PA5)".

If no single-seam PA5 reaches that named check (for example, the fault fails an earlier check or breaks the build after one scoped retry), do not stop again. Record MA5 as a disclosed, non-equivalent survivor under the R6 precedent and this ruling, add it to CF-A2M-1's combined-mutant follow-up list, and continue to the lifecycle and the PR.

Standing rule for the rest of Step 3 (B included): a survivor that deletes an assertion is handled this way without a new stop. Any other survivor still stops for Root.

## 2026-10-28 Root ruling: #2349 first-rolls finding (GPT F1 = Opus F1)

Facts: both reviews of head 5dd8d6aa9 independently found that coop-first-rolls-captured does not check the FIRST post-restart dice-producing batch.
- The row accepts only AdvancePhase replies of type initiative_rolled, attack_resolved or physical_attack_resolved.
- The product stamps the captured rolls and the intentId on the first event of a command batch. For an attack batch that is attack_locked (built run: intent coop-gm-2-2, attack_locked seq 15, rolls [3,1]).
- So the row skipped that batch and validated the turn-2 initiative_rolled (seq 34).
- The registered acceptance (units.json L1-SMOKE-A2, A3) requires the first post-restart dice-producing event. Opus confirmed from the database that the first batch's rolls were in fact captured; the harness just never asserts it.

Ruling: fix it in this PR. The disclose-and-carry option is rejected because the acceptance is registered and the fix is small.
1. Change the selection in the cases leaf so that:
   - the row validates the earliest post-restart dice-producing batch: its first event, carrying the captured rolls and the accepted intentId;
   - the row fails, rather than skipping ahead, if an earlier batch with a dice resolution event lacks captured rolls on its first event.
   Keep the change minimal and put the selection in an exported pure function so it can be unit-tested. This is a disclosed G-A3 deviation from the frozen draftSha256: list it with the old and new sha256, re-measure, and re-check against G-A8 (option A must stay at or under 500).
2. Node falsifiers in the test leaf (which is exempt):
   - an earlier attack batch with missing rolls and a later valid initiative batch must fail;
   - an earlier attack batch with valid rolls must be the one selected.
   Add pure mutants for the new function, and all of them must be killed.
3. Run a new full built run on the new head (--build, all 26 cases). It becomes the registered GREEN built run; the 5dd8d6aa9-era run is disclosed as superseded. CF-A2FP-2 applies as before.
4. Rerun MA4 on the new image. The MA1/PA1 and MA5/PA5 pairings and MA2 and MA3 are not rerun: their rows' bytes are unchanged. Disclose that, and record their leaf hash as the pre-fix bytes.
5. Also apply Opus F2 (MA2-MA5 used the owned-rows-only harness on a pristine rebuild; disclose), F3 (MA4 tests a missing replay event, not a wrong one; the empty-rolls half is covered only by pure R2), F4 (contributor block in the local receipt: GPT gpt-6.1-sol made commits 1-4, Claude Sonnet made 5-6 after the content-filter handover; one line in the PR body; no history rewrite), INFO-3 (ma3 sourceContext cites the co-op early return at ServerMatchHostIntent.ts:567) and INFO-5 (the PR body's description of 2581096fb).
6. U38 picking up CF-A2-1 (Opus INFO-2) is routed in the A2 closure PR's carry-forward, not by editing U38 here.
